data.title: A photo-caged cross-linker for identifying protein-protein interactions
data.projectDescription: In recent years cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) as a tool to study protein-protein interactions (PPIs) has undergone significant improvements, which were mainly propelled by the emergence of novel crosslinkers and the development and implementation of advanced analysis workflows. Despite these recent advancements, addressing PPIs in the cell by XL-MS remains a substantial challenge. Some of the current limitations are linked to a comparable poor membrane permeability of most crosslinkers and their limited efficiency to traverse the cellular membrane. To address this problem, we have designed and synthesized a novel crosslinker based on the chemical o-nitrobenzylester (o-NBE) group, which enhances the hydrophobic properties of the cross-linker.
data.sampleProcessingProtocol: 100 µg of Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) at a concentration of 1 µg/µl was mixed with the crosslinker o-Nitrosobenzaldehyde (o-NBE) at a final concentration of 2mM. The reaction was allowed to proceed over time intervals of 0 minutes, 10 minutes, 20 minutes and 30 minutes, using 365nm UV light (Thorlabs M365L2, 190 mW (min). Following UV-light activation, the crosslinked samples were incubated at 37°C under continuous shaking at 650 rpm for 3 hours in a Thermomixer (Eppendorf) before sodium triacetoxyhydroborate (STAB) at a concentration of 10 mM was added for 20 minutes to quench the reaction by reduction.  In-gel digest was performed as previously described. The crosslinked samples were separated by SDS-PAGE and stained overnight. Protein bands were excised into small segments of around 1 cm² and destained with a 50/50 (v/v) solution of acetonitrile (ACN) and 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate (ABi) and incubated for 15 minutes at 37°C at 650 rpm. Subsequently, protein bands were reduced in 100 mM NH₄HCO3, 10 mM DTT for 30 min at 56° C, alkylated in 100 mM NH₄HCO3, 55 mM iodoacetamide for 20 min at 23° C in the dark, and digested with 13ng/µl trypsin (Promega, sequencing grade) in 10 mM 100 mM NH₄HCO3, 10% ACN for 2 h on ice, followed by 18 h at 37° C. Samples were extracted and dried using a SpeedVac. Dried peptides were re-suspended in 0.1% TFA for 15 min at 37° C and adjusted to pH <3 with TFA. The peptides were loaded onto Pierce C18 SpinTip columns (Thermo, 10 µg) and desalted according to protocol. Crosslinked peptides were separated on an EASY-nLC 1200 system (Thermo Scientific) at a flow rate of 300 nl/min over a 60 min gradient elution (5 % acetonitrile in 0.1 % formic acid for 4 min, 5 % - 35 % acetonitrile in 0.1% formic acid in 55 min, 35 % - 80 % acetonitrile in 1 min) and measured on a Orbitrap Fusion Tribrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Electron, San Jose, CA). Full scan mass spectra were acquired in the Orbitrap at a resolution of 120,000, a scan range of 400–1600 m/z, and a maximum injection time of 50 ms. Precursor ions with charge states 3-8 were fragmented by CID at 35 % collision in a data dependent mode. The exclusion duration of dynamic exclusion is 60s and spectra were analyzed in the ion trap with rapid scan rate.
data.dataProcessingProtocol: Analysis of MS data was conducted using Proteome Discoverer 2.4 (Thermo Scientific). The XlinkX mode was applied for the identification of cross-linked peptides, while the SEQUEST HT search engine was employed for the detection of unmodified and dead-end-modified peptides. The following setting were chosen: acquisition strategy “non-cleavable” and a minimum S/N value of 1.5. The calculated mass of the crosslinker was set at 550.206366 Da (product 1), 552.22201 Da (product 2) and 554.237664 Da (product 3), respectively and the primary reaction assumed to be with lysines. The maximum missed cleavage was set to 2 and minimum peptide length was 5. Dead-end-modified peptides (i.e. where o-NBE reacted only one side with an amino acid) were assumed to contain multiple functional groups on the non-reacted side including a reduced hydroxyl group (+572.248Da), aldehyde group(+570.233Da) and carboxylic acid group (+586.227Da). These modifications have been collectively introduced as dynamic modifications, alongside methionine oxidation (+15.996 Da) and acetylation of the N-terminus (+42.011 Da). Carbamidomethylation (+57.021 Da) was employed as a static modification for cysteine in the analysis. The Uniprot P02769 fasta file of BSA was used and a 0.05 FDR cut off in the percolator mode chosen.
